verses.text: But now they make fun of me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would not have put with my sheepdogs.
What use was their strength to me? Their strength was gone.
They were thin from hunger and want. They wandered the dry land at night, in empty and ruined places.
They picked salty plants among the bushes and ate the roots of broom trees.
They were driven away from other people, who shouted at them as if they were thieves.
They had to live in dry stream beds, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
They howled like animals among the bushes and huddled together under the weeds.
They were worthless people, the children of nobodies, driven out of the land with whips.
And now they make fun of me in their songs. I have become a joke to them.
They hate me and stay away from me. They do not even hold back from spitting in my face.
Because God has cut my bowstring and made me suffer, they do whatever they want to me.
On my right side a mob attacks me. They trip me up and build ramps to attack me.
They block my path and try to destroy me, and no one stops them.
They come at me as if through a wide gap in a wall. They roll over me in the ruins.
Terrors overwhelm me. My honor is blown away like the wind, and my safety vanishes like a cloud.
Now my life is draining out of me. Days of suffering have taken hold of me.
At night my bones ache, and the gnawing pain never rests.
With great force God grabs my clothing. He holds me by the collar of my shirt.
He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer. I stand up, but you only look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me. You attack me with all your strength.
You lift me up and let the wind carry me away. You toss me around in the storm.
I know you will bring me down to death, to the place where all living things must go.
Surely no one would strike a man who is ruined and crying for help in his trouble.
Didn't I cry for those who were in trouble? Didn't I feel sad for the poor?
But when I hoped for good, evil came. When I looked for light, darkness came.
My insides are churning and never rest. Days of suffering face me.
I walk around in darkness, without sunlight. I stand up in public and cry for help.
I have become a brother of jackals and a friend of ostriches.
My skin turns black and peels off. My body burns with fever.
My harp plays only sad songs, and my flute only the sound of crying.
